# Plaid

Plaid's bank-connectivity and financial-data platform, in two parts: the REST API (`api`) for Link, Items, Auth, Balance, Transactions, Identity, Investments, Liabilities, Income, Transfer, Signal and the rest, and the Dashboard MCP server (`mcp`) for read-only Production diagnostics and analytics (Item debugging, Link conversion, usage and API volumes, team discovery). The catalog target "Plaid MCP" is the same product, so it is mounted here under `mcp`.

## Interfaces

- `api`: Plaid's official OpenAPI document, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plaid/plaid-openapi/master/2020-09-14.yml (maintained by Plaid in `plaid/plaid-openapi`). 335 tools. Plaid's API is POST-only RPC: operations ending in get, list, search or sync run without approval, all others ask for approval. The spec's Plaid-Version header requirement is dropped, so Plaid serves its default API version.
- `mcp`: Plaid's official Dashboard MCP server, `https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/` (streamable HTTP). Tools: `plaid_debug_item`, `plaid_get_link_analytics`, `plaid_get_tools_introduction`, `plaid_get_usages`, `plaid_list_teams`. Tools not marked read-only ask for approval.

## Auth

- REST API, client ID and secret: copy them from Team Settings > Keys in the [Plaid Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/developers/keys). Enter the environment (`production` or `sandbox`) with them; it is fixed per connected account, so connect once per environment. Credentials are sent as `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` and `PLAID-SECRET` headers only to the matching Plaid host. The health check calls the read-only `/institutions/get`.
- Dashboard MCP, Production keys: enter the same client ID and **Production** secret from Team Settings > Keys. Plaid requires Production approval for at least one product. The host uses Plaid's documented `client_credentials` grant at `https://production.plaid.com/oauth/token`, requesting only `mcp:dashboard`. It retains the grant and renews the 15-minute access token; no browser sign-in, OAuth app registration or manually pasted access token is needed. See [Plaid's Dashboard MCP guide](https://plaid.com/docs/resources/mcp/) and [OAuth API reference](https://plaid.com/docs/api/oauth/).
- Dashboard MCP, browser OAuth: the existing discovered OAuth method remains available for clients using Plaid's authorization page. Existing accounts and their original sign-in method are preserved.

REST and MCP remain separate account requirements here. This change does not automatically reuse a saved REST key pair. In particular, a Sandbox REST connection is never automatically exchanged against Production. MCP access tokens go only to `api.dashboard.plaid.com`; the client ID and secret are handled by the host's native OAuth flow, not exposed to app tools.

## Known gaps

- 16 operations are skipped because they use a different authentication scheme than the client ID and secret.
- The REST API spec's operations are all served from the production or sandbox host; the retired `development` environment is not offered.
- The MCP server only works with Production data and requires Production approval for a Plaid product. Plaid labels it under active development.
- Link tokens and Link UI flows need a client application; the API tools only create tokens.

import type { OpenapiToolNamesOptions } from "apps/openapi";

// Plaid's official OpenAPI document. It lists production and sandbox servers; index.ts pins the
// account's own environment as the only origin that receives credentials.
export const environments = {
  production: "https://production.plaid.com",
  sandbox: "https://sandbox.plaid.com",
} as const;

// The array value is valid at runtime; the declared patch type only admits objects.
const patches = [
  { op: "replace", path: "/security", value: [{ clientId: [], secret: [] }] },
] as unknown as NonNullable<OpenapiToolNamesOptions["patches"]>;

  source: { url: "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plaid/plaid-openapi/master/2020-09-14.yml" },
  allowedOrigin: environments.production,
  baseUrl: environments.production,
  securitySchemes: {
    clientId: { type: "apiKey", in: "header", name: "PLAID-CLIENT-ID" },
    secret: { type: "apiKey", in: "header", name: "PLAID-SECRET" },
  },
  methods: {
    apiKey: [
      { scheme: "clientId", field: "client_id", part: "value", prefix: "" },
      { scheme: "secret", field: "secret", part: "value", prefix: "" },
    ],
  },
  // Every operation also lists the optional Plaid-Version header scheme; drop it so keys alone authorize
  // operations (Plaid then serves its default API version).
  patches,
  kinds,
  oauth: [],
} satisfies OpenapiToolNamesOptions;
